items.title: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach
items.snippet: 1Password has disclosed a data breach after a an employee's corporate GitHub account was hacked and used to deploy malicious code to the company's backend services to steal customer data. [...]
items.summary: 1Password disclosed that an employee's corporate GitHub account was hacked and used to deploy malicious code to backend services and steal customer data.
items.why: Review corporate GitHub access and deployment activity for unauthorized use.

items.title: NordVPN Black Friday Deal: Get 78% off VPN plans in 2026

items.title: Fake paid expert interviews impersonate brands to steal Google logins
items.snippet: An ongoing phishing campaign dubbed "GoodGuys" impersonates major brands, including Google, Nvidia, Accenture, and SpaceX, to steal corporate Google and Okta credentials using fake invitations to paid expert interviews and webinars. [...]
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports that the GoodGuys phishing campaign impersonates major brands with fake paid interview and webinar invitations to steal corporate Google and Okta credentials.
items.why: Train staff to verify interview invitations and check login requests before entering corporate credentials.

items.title: Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension
items.snippet: The Remus infostealer is stealing Gmail messages through a stealthy malicious Chrome extension, a capability the malware operators marketed as a zero-day exploit in Google's email service. [...]
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports that the Remus infostealer uses a malicious Chrome extension to steal Gmail messages; operators marketed the capability as a Google email zero-day.
items.why: Review Chrome extensions and investigate unexpected access to Gmail messages.

items.title: SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
items.snippet: A new version of the SYS01 infostealer malware delivered through Meta ads is enrolling browsers into enterprise-style management to force the installation of an extension that steals sensitive data, including Gmail and Outlook emails. [...]
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports that a SYS01 infostealer version delivered through Meta ads enrolls browsers in enterprise-style management and installs an extension to steal Gmail and Outlook emails.
items.why: Check browser management enrollment, extensions, and email access for unexpected changes.

learn.explainer: An infostealer is malware designed to take information from a device or account. Here, Remus and SYS01 are described as stealing email messages.
An autonomous underwater vehicle is an underwater system designed to operate without continuous direct control. The item describes a modular vehicle designed for rapid production.

Attribution is the process of identifying who was responsible for an event. In the Kuwait strike report, Iran denies responsibility, while Italy's foreign ministry identifies the victims as Rheinmetall technicians.

analysis.headline: Credential Risks and Regional Uncertainty in Focus
paragraphs: The reported 1Password breach, involving a compromised employee GitHub account and malicious code deployed to backend services, shows a different route to customer data. Across these accounts, trust in platforms, code, and account access is a common concern. Analysts should distinguish disclosed details from gaps, including FIFA’s unspecified timing and scope.

Beyond cyber, reports describe a deadly strike in Kuwait with responsibility denied by Iran, and hardship for displaced Palestinians during winter rains. A discussion links Ukraine’s war to Europe’s outlook on space, while EU leaders debate a long-term budget. Watch for verified updates on attribution, conditions, and policy decisions.
takeaways: Treat credential theft and malicious extensions as connected access risks.
Separate confirmed incident details from unreported scope or disputed attribution.
Track how conflict, humanitarian conditions, and policy debates shape regional analysis.
